description.value: Roedde House Museum is a meticulously restored 1893 Queen Anne Revival home designed by architect Francis Rattenbury, now preserving the domestic world of Vancouver's first bookbinder, Gustav Roedde. Unlike many heritage houses, all eleven furnished rooms are fully accessible to visitors rather than roped off, with self-guided and docent-led tours available in eight languages. Located in the West End's Barclay Heritage Square, it also hosts a regular Jazz in the Parlour series and rotating exhibits, making it a cultural landmark a short ride from the Stanley Park seawall.

bike_parking_detail: 1 rack within 100m: wall_loops (3 spaces) at 48m. Total: 3 spaces.

Neither the website nor OSM tags mention bike parking, bike racks, washrooms, or water refill explicitly, so all cycling-specific required criteria remain null. OSM wheelchair=yes is partially corroborated by the website noting 'Wheelchair Accessible Admission' for the ground floor only.
concerns: Phone number 604.684.7040 is sourced from the website only; OSM has no phone field for cross-checking.
OSM address lacked postal code; full postal code V6G 1J6 taken from website contact page.
Wheelchair accessibility is ground-floor only per website ('Wheelchair Accessible Admission: ground floor only'), which nuances the OSM wheelchair=yes tag.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate, active heritage attraction well-placed for cycling tourists near Stanley Park, but none of the three required criteria (bike parking, water refill, washrooms) can be confirmed from the website or OSM tags. On-site verification is needed before a full WWC listing can be justified.
enrichment_extras.notes: Tea & Tour is a monthly event (last Sunday of each month, suspended April–May 2026) that includes refreshments, but this is a ticketed event rather than a standing cafe or food service.
